title: Structure of the Picard group of a proper curve
statement:
Let $C$ be a proper smooth connected curve over
algebraically closed $k$. The degree sequence

$$
0\longrightarrow\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Pic}(C)\xrightarrow{\ \deg\ }\mathbf Z\longrightarrow0
$$

splits (the degree map is surjective since a $k$-rational point
gives a degree-one class), hence

$$
\operatorname{Pic}(C)\cong\mathbf Z\oplus\operatorname{Pic}^0(C).
$$

proof.text: **The degree is surjective, with an explicit preimage of $1$.** Let $C$ be a proper smooth connected curve over the algebraically closed field $k$ ([def-sc-curves]). By [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings] (2), $C$ has a closed point $P$. Since $C$ is of finite type over $k$ and $k$ is algebraically closed, $k\to\kappa(P)$ is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], so $P$ is a $k$-rational point (this is the place where the blueprint invokes the Nullstellensatz; with the degree $\deg\sum n_Q[Q]=\sum n_Q$ of [def-sc-divisor] it is not even needed, and with the weighted degree $\sum n_Q[\kappa(Q):k]$ of the unit sketch it gives the same value). The divisor $[P]\in\operatorname{Div}(C)$ has $\deg[P]=1$ by the definition of the degree of a divisor ([def-sc-divisor]). The degree on $\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ is, by [def-sc-pic0], the degree of divisors transported along the isomorphism of abelian groups $\operatorname{Cl}(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Pic}(C)$, $D\mapsto[\mathcal O_C(D)]$ of [lem-sc-divisor-class-curve]; it is well defined because principal divisors have degree $0$ ([lem-sc-deg-principal-zero]), and it is a homomorphism of groups, since $D\mapsto\deg D=\sum n_Q$ is additive on $\operatorname{Div}(C)$ and the identification with $\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ is a group isomorphism. Put $\lambda:=[\mathcal O_C(P)]\in\operatorname{Pic}(C)$. Then $\deg\lambda=\deg[P]=1$, and for $n\in\mathbf Z$, $\deg(\lambda^{\otimes n})=\deg[\mathcal O_C(nP)]=\deg(n[P])=n$. Hence $\deg:\operatorname{Pic}(C)\to\mathbf Z$ is surjective, and $s:\mathbf Z\to\operatorname{Pic}(C)$, $n\mapsto\lambda^{\otimes n}=[\mathcal O_C(nP)]$, is a group homomorphism with $\deg\circ s=\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf Z}$. (Any closed point $P$ may be used; citers use this freedom to pick $P$.)

**Exactness and the splitting.** Write the group law of $\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ additively. By definition $\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)=\ker(\deg)$ ([def-sc-pic0]), so $0\to\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Pic}(C)\xrightarrow{\deg}\mathbf Z$ is exact (injectivity of the inclusion and exactness in the middle are the definition of a kernel), and step 1 gives exactness at $\mathbf Z$. With the section $s$ of step 1 define
$$\Phi:\operatorname{Pic}(C)\to\mathbf Z\oplus\operatorname{Pic}^0(C),\qquad x\mapsto\bigl(\deg x,\ x-s(\deg x)\bigr),$$
which lands in $\mathbf Z\oplus\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$ because $\deg(x-s(\deg x))=\deg x-\deg x=0$, and is a homomorphism because $\deg$ and $s$ are. Its inverse is $\Psi(n,y)=s(n)+y$: $\Psi\Phi(x)=s(\deg x)+x-s(\deg x)=x$, and $\Phi\Psi(n,y)=(n+\deg y,\ s(n)+y-s(n))=(n,y)$ since $\deg y=0$. So $\Phi$ is an isomorphism $\operatorname{Pic}(C)\cong\mathbf Z\oplus\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$ whose first component is $\deg$ and which restricts to the identity on $\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$, i.e. the sequence splits. (This is the elementary fact that a short exact sequence of abelian groups ending in the free group $\mathbf Z$ splits; in Mathlib it is the $R=\mathbf Z$ case of `Function.Exact.splitSurjectiveEquiv`, Mathlib/Algebra/Exact/Basic.lean line 381, applied to the section $s$.)

Its own term has no sorry, but walking the 'd' lists of local/sorry_map_slopmaster2_71d63dcf.jsonl.gz reaches three sorried declarations, all through picDegreeHom._proof_2 (the proof that the cohomological degree χ(L)-χ(O) is a homomorphism): Modules.subsingleton_H_of_topologicalKrullDim_lt (Cohomology/EulerChar 64-73), Modules.finite_sections_higherDirectImage (Cohomology/DirectImage 617-632; node lem-pc-coherent-hi), Modules.exists_addEquiv_sections_higherDirectImage_H (Cohomology/DirectImage 307-324).
